text:
24-hour news summary.

1 — Tinygrad says the future depends on an unspecified trend's direction. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5824)
2 — Microsoft plans multi-gigawatt Maia deployments in 2027, claiming Maia 300 beats GPUs on tokens per watt by 40%. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5827)
3 — Phoronix reports Torvalds is using Claude Code for a major Linux kernel performance improvement. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5828)
4 — Hesamation claims DeepMind's AlphaProof Nexus solved nine Erdős problems, with peer-reviewed, Lean-checked results. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5829)
5 — Qwen says QwenGyre accelerates long-horizon agent RL up to 1.85× through elastic GPU scheduling. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5830)
6 — The Information reportedly says Katzenberg's startup is negotiating customizable Sora access for OpenAI equity. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5831)
7 — Rohan Paul reports AWS–HSBC's Double Ratchet evolves agent graders from ten labeled examples. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5832)
8 — Zuckerberg introduces Muse Wonder, claiming frontier performance for personal and professional agents. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5835)
9 — Z.ai introduces GLM-Legal for legal workflows, claiming parity with frontier models on legal benchmarks. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5836)
10 — Kimmonismus reports Muse Wonder scores 56 on AA's Intelligence Index, two points behind Opus 5.5. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5837)
11 — Alexandr Wang credits Muse Wonder's progress to over a year of research and scaled pretraining and RL. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5838)
12 — Streaming Code World Model's team releases code and weights, reporting 5.1 seconds per video chunk on an H200. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5839)
13 — SubQ launches Snap, advertising 384K-token multimodal context and $0.05 per million input tokens. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5840)
14 — Blueprints AI says it generates permit-ready construction plans from sketches or PDFs in minutes. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5841)
15 — Rohan Paul reports Nvidia predicts post-training coding skill by scoring base models on decisive, test-passing edits. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5842)
16 — Early tester boneGPT praises Muse Wonder's creativity and technical performance, offering access through Slopcannon. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5843)
17 — Artificial Analysis launches its FrontierCode 1.1 leaderboard, led by Opus 5.5 at 52%. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5844)
18 — Kled launches a lab aiming to train competitive models solely on data from its 600,000-plus contributors. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5845)
19 — Zilan Qian quotes Unitree's CEO praising GPT-6 robot pilots while noting generalization and efficiency gaps. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5846)
20 — ReadMe introduces Restless to track agent API requests and provide corrective guidance in error responses. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5847)
21 — Microsoft Research presents StudentSim to evaluate AI tutors through simulated learner interactions. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5848)
22 — Scaling01 quotes Anthropic warning small models may soon self-replicate on commercial IoT devices. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5849)
23 — Airtable announces major layoffs, arguing smaller teams ship better, alongside planned product and infrastructure upgrades. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5850)
24 — MaxBlade reports Muse Wonder lagged Opus 5.5 on a game-building test and quickly exhausted subscription allowances. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5851)
25 — Dan Shipper reports Muse Wonder scored 52% versus GPT-Sol 6.1's 71% on his senior-engineer benchmark. (https://t.me/dlmehr/5852)

--Hermes.
